definition: Mamba is a deep learning architecture focused on sequence modeling.
details: It was developed by two researchers Albert Gu from Carnegie Mellon University and Tri Dao from Princeton University to address some limitations of transformer models, especially in processing long sequences, and it is based on the Structured State Space sequence (S4) model.

explainer.lead: Mamba is a sequence-modeling architecture built to handle long sequences that strain transformer models. It matters because long-sequence processing is a recurring bottleneck in modern AI.

tiers.eli5: Think of reading a very long book: instead of re-reading every earlier page each time you reach a new one, you carry a running summary.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use Mamba as an alternative sequence backbone when attention over long inputs gets costly. The pitfall is assuming it behaves like a transformer; its state-based processing changes how you reason about long-range recall.
tiers.paperLevel: Mamba is a deep learning architecture for sequence modeling, based on the Structured State Space sequence (S4) model, developed by Albert Gu (Carnegie Mellon University) and Tri Dao (Princeton University). It was proposed to address limitations of transformer models, especially in processing long sequences.

explainer.example: A team modeling very long documents swaps a transformer for a Mamba-based model to avoid the cost of attention across the full sequence.
